text.arabic_uthmani: قُلْ إِن ضَلَلْتُ فَإِنَّمَآ أَضِلُّ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِى ۖ وَإِنِ ٱهْتَدَيْتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِىٓ إِلَىَّ رَبِّىٓ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعٌۭ قَرِيبٌۭ

words.gloss_range: commanded saying that frames the whole quoted accountability argument
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, public claim, and articulated stance; local Form I imperative selects commissioned utterance
words.prose: {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) makes the whole ayah a commissioned utterance, not private self-analysis: the speaker is instructed to voice both the error condition and the guidance condition. The q-w-l field gives that speech public accountability, so liability and guidance become a stated position that can be heard and tested. Its place after 34:49 keeps the command chain moving from truth’s arrival to first-person accountability, while the opening qāf returns at the close in {{ar:قَرِيبٌۭ}} ({{tr:qarībun}}), so the spoken answer ends in nearness rather than autonomy.

topics.headline: command frames the whole answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the self-accounting is an authorized public answer placed in the messenger’s mouth, not a private aside.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a singular imperative introducing the quoted utterance, so both conditionals fall under the command.

topics.headline: speech becomes accountable stance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command externalizes the liability/guidance distinction as audible doctrine rather than leaving it as inward reasoning.
topics.reason: The speech-root rows are locally supported by the imperative and by the ayah’s quoted argumentative content.

topics.headline: command chain points beyond the speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 34:50 continues the nearby command sequence after 34:49, but now routes the speaker’s stance under the Lord who reveals.
topics.reason: The rows tie the opening command to r-b-b cooccurrence, same-surah command recurrence, and the qāf bookend with the final nearness predicate.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle opening the adverse hypothetical
words.prose: {{ar:إِن}} ({{tr:in}}) suspends the adverse claim as a condition: even if straying is granted, it is not narrated as the speaker’s actual settled identity. Its scope reaches forward to the result and restriction, so the first half answers accusation by bounding the possible case before the guidance half begins. The small particle therefore lets the ayah start with the hostile possibility while keeping that possibility grammatically controlled.

topics.headline: adverse claim held as condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first clause grants an adverse possibility for argument without turning it into a direct confession.
topics.reason: The conditional particle opens the protasis and its answer is the following fā-marked apodosis.

topics.headline: accusation bounded before guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah handles the accusation first, then turns to the positive source of guidance.
topics.reason: The ordering rows are coherent with the two conditional frames and are not contradicted by reference evidence.

words.gloss_range: first-person perfect straying inside a conditional, not a simple confession
words.root_gloss_range: path-loss, error, going astray, and disappearance; local Form I selects intransitive self-straying, not causing others to stray

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: ongoing straying verb in the first answer

words.prose: {{ar:ضَلَلْتُ}} ({{tr:ḍalaltu}}) gives error a completed-state form inside a conditional, so the ayah can analyze liability without making straying the speaker’s present identity. The root’s path-loss image makes the possible error a loss of orientation, but the Form I intransitive shape keeps it as the speaker’s own straying rather than causative misleading of others. The reported vocalic variants test the sound shape without changing that first-person conditional frame. The same root then returns in {{ar:أَضِلُّ}} ({{tr:aḍillu}}), shifting from completed hypothetical state to ongoing consequence, while parallels such as 17:15 and 10:108 support the rule that straying falls back on the self.

topics.headline: completed state without actuality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that completed-form straying is examined under an if-frame, not asserted as a simple past self-description.
topics.reason: The QAC perfect form is inside the conditional protasis, and the following imperfect consequence creates an aspect movement.

topics.headline: self-straying path image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the error is pictured as the speaker’s own loss of orientation, not as an act of misleading others.
topics.reason: The local Form I intransitive verb and absence of direct object block causative agency while preserving the path-loss field.

topics.headline: variant pressure preserves the frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that reported vocalic variants test the sound shape but do not change the first-person conditional error frame.
topics.reason: Variant evidence can serve as apparatus, but the canonical local parse remains the Form I first-person perfect in the conditional.

topics.headline: general liability made first-person
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that broader guidance/error doctrine, including 34:24 and 17:15, is compressed into first-person accountability after 34:49.
topics.reason: The cited parallels and boundary rows reinforce the local self-liability frame without controlling the grammar.

topics.headline: condition echoes into consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated ḍ-l-l sound makes error seem to continue into its own self-contained consequence.
topics.reason: The echo between the protasis verb and apodosis verb is directly present in the local surface sequence.

words.gloss_range: result link introducing the first conditional answer

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: restrictive particle in the first answer

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the bridge from the first condition to its answer. Because the answer begins with {{ar:إِنَّمَا}} ({{tr:innamā}}), the result marker makes the boundary explicit and ties restriction directly to the granted error case. Its fusion in {{ar:فَإِنَّمَا}} ({{tr:fa-innamā}}) compresses consequence and exclusivity, so there is no pause between possible straying and bounded liability.

topics.headline: result marker before restriction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the restrictive answer is syntactically tied to the error condition, not added as a loose comment.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies words 4-8 as the answer to the first protasis.

topics.headline: no gap before liability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how quickly the granted error case is converted into a confined consequence.
topics.reason: The result particle is fused orthographically to the restrictive particle, supporting the compact consequence reading.

words.gloss_range: restrictive particle confining the consequence of error
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّمَا}} ({{tr:innamā}}) is the first half’s narrowing device: if error is granted, its consequence is confined to the speaker’s own self. The composite particle carries assertion and exclusion together, so the clause does more than add “only”; it blocks the inference that the source of guidance, the message, or the audience is damaged by the hypothetical error. It also finishes the first conditional half as a contained liability unit before the guidance condition opens.

topics.headline: error confined to self
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the possible error is fenced off from revelation and Lordship before guidance is explained.
topics.reason: The restrictive particle governs the apodosis that lands on the self-burden phrase.

topics.headline: assertion converted into exclusivity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the restriction is forceful and formal, not merely an optional paraphrase of “only.”
topics.reason: The particle is analyzed as inna plus mā kāffah, and the recitational lengthening row reinforces the hinge without changing grammar.

topics.headline: bounded accountability before guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first conditional is closed as self-burden before the ayah can assign guidance to another source.
topics.reason: The restriction plus adverse prepositional endpoint makes the first half a compact accountability unit.

words.gloss_range: first-person imperfect straying as ongoing self-borne consequence
words.root_gloss_range: path-loss and misdirection field; local Form I and lack of object keep the action intransitive rather than causative

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: restrictive particle in the first answer

words.prose: {{ar:أَضِلُّ}} ({{tr:aḍillu}}) repeats the error root inside the restricted answer, but now as an imperfect ongoing state. The verb is boxed between {{ar:إِنَّمَا}} ({{tr:innamā}}) and {{ar:عَلَىٰ نَفْسِى}} ({{tr:ʿalā nafsī}}), so continued straying cannot escape into someone else’s harm. Its Form I shape and lack of direct object keep the meaning at “I stray,” not “I mislead,” while the local stray-to-self pattern is sharpened by parallels such as 10:108 and 39:41. The ḍ-l-l echo and doubled liquid sound make the consequence feel like the condition’s own lingering continuation.

topics.headline: imperfect consequence boxed in
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a possible completed error becomes an ongoing consequence, but only inside the restriction and self-burden frame.
topics.reason: The imperfect apodosis verb is placed after the restrictive particle and before the adverse prepositional endpoint.

topics.headline: straying not misleading others
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause blocks the accusation of transmitting error to others: the verb has no direct object and is not the causative form.
topics.reason: QAC notes the form as first-person Form I in the apodosis; attachment supplies the prepositional complement, not a direct object.

topics.headline: recognized stray-to-self frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local phrase participates in a broader stray-to-self pattern while standing opposite the guidance condition.
topics.reason: The cooccurrence and parallels such as 10:108 and 39:41 support the local self-liability frame.

topics.headline: error lingers in repeated sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated ḍ-l-l sequence makes the consequence sound like a continuation of the same deviation.
topics.reason: The echo is directly visible between the protasis and apodosis verbs; the sound rows add acoustic payoff without changing lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: preposition of adverse burden upon the self
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) chooses an adverse burden frame for the consequence. The self is not merely the inner location of error and not the instrument of error; it is the surface on which the burden falls. The preposition remains visible between the verb and {{ar:نَفْسِى}} ({{tr:nafsī}}), completing the first answer with a pressure-bearing endpoint and a recognizable self-liability formula before the second conditional begins.

topics.headline: upon the self, not for or by it
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition turns error into liability against the self rather than benefit, means, or neutral inwardness.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows the preposition governing the self as the complement of the straying verb.

topics.headline: spatial pressure becomes moral load
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the embodied burden image: error presses upon a defined endpoint.
topics.reason: The physical superposition field survives locally as adverse liability, while the separate preposition makes the relation explicit.

topics.headline: prepositional endpoint closes the first half
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first conditional answer lands on a familiar self-liability formula before guidance opens.
topics.reason: The row’s liability-formula claim is supported by the local phrase and by the conditional boundary.

words.gloss_range: my own self as the definite endpoint of liability
words.root_gloss_range: self, person, soul, life, breath, and agency; local possessed singular selects the accountable self
words.prose: {{ar:نَفْسِى}} ({{tr:nafsī}}) names the exact bearer of the burden: the speaker’s own self. Its possessed singular form makes the endpoint definite and non-transferable, while its genitive case shows that it is governed by {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}). The n-f-s field keeps liability attached to the living person, not an abstract theory, while parallels such as 17:15 and 39:41 show the recurring stray-to-self rule being personalized here. The word’s position closes the first conditional half before {{ar:رَبِّىٓ}} ({{tr:rabbī}}) later names the opposite first-person pole: my self bears error, my Lord supplies guidance.

topics.headline: my self as governed endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that liability is neither collective nor vague: it is grammatically pinned to the speaker’s own self.
topics.reason: The noun is singular with a first-person suffix and is governed by the adverse preposition.

topics.headline: self field thickens the endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the endpoint is the speaker as living person and accountable self, while the adjacent breath-token sense is not the local sense.
topics.reason: The root field includes breath and life, but QAC and context select the accountable self here.

topics.headline: recurring rule personalized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a recurring stray-to-self rule, including 17:15 and 39:41, is converted into a first-person endpoint after the truth/falsehood verdict of 34:49.
topics.reason: The local phrase matches the self-liability pattern and closes the first half before the guidance half.

topics.headline: possessive endpoints divide roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the matched first-person suffixes do opposite work: my self receives burden, my Lord gives guidance.
topics.reason: The later possessive Lord phrase is syntactically the revealer, making the polarity locally grounded.

words.gloss_range: coordinator opening the matched guidance conditional
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does not merely continue the sentence; it opens a fresh conditional counterpart by attaching to the second {{ar:إِنِ}} ({{tr:ini}}). Because the particle itself is simple coordination, the contrast must arise from the paired meanings: error versus guidance, self-burden versus revealed source. The hinge keeps the two if-frames joined while preserving the first half’s completed liability boundary.

topics.headline: coordination opens a second if-frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is not a loose afterthought but a parallel conditional frame coordinated with the error frame.
topics.reason: The conjunction is attached to a repeated conditional particle, which starts the second protasis.

topics.headline: contrast carried by the clauses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah uses coordination rather than an explicit adversative, making the opposed outcomes do the contrastive work.
topics.reason: The two complete if-frames are coordinated, and the recitational hinge supports the turn without changing syntax.

topics.headline: opposite endpoints distributed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the architecture: error is sent to self-burden, guidance to revelation from the Lord.
topics.reason: The attachment profile identifies two matched conditional apodoses with different endpoints.

words.gloss_range: second conditional particle, with liaison vowel before the guided-state verb
words.prose: {{ar:إِنِ}} ({{tr:ini}}) mirrors the first conditional particle while smoothing into {{ar:ٱهْتَدَيْتُ}} ({{tr:ihtadaytu}}) through the liaison vowel. The effect is important: even the positive state is placed under a disciplined if-frame, so the speaker does not boast of guidance before the answer names its means. Across the boundary from 34:49’s proclamation, the repeated conditionals make the argument test both possibilities without retreating from the certainty of truth.

topics.headline: second condition mirrors the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance receives equal syntactic discipline with error before its source is named.
topics.reason: The particle opens the second protasis and balances the first conditional frame.

topics.headline: kasra binds particle to verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surface changes for recitational liaison while the particle’s conditional identity remains the same.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the form as the conditional particle with kasra before hamzat al-waṣl.

topics.headline: certainty becomes tested reasoning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 34:50 answers objections through hypothetical structure after 34:49’s factual proclamation.
topics.reason: The boundary rows are compatible with the repeated conditional syntax and do not override the local parse.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII first-person guided state whose means is immediately displaced to revelation
words.root_gloss_range: guiding, showing a route, reaching a way, gift-offering, and seeking guidance; local Form VIII selects received/internalized orientation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: guidance answer opening through what is revealed

words.prose: {{ar:ٱهْتَدَيْتُ}} ({{tr:ihtadaytu}}) names a real guided state, but its Form VIII profile makes it received and internalized rather than self-authored. The perfect form presents achieved orientation inside the conditional, then the apodosis immediately moves to {{ar:فَبِمَا يُوحِىٓ}} ({{tr:fa-bimā yūḥī}}), refusing to let guidance stand as autonomous credit. The h-d-y field answers the repeated ḍ-l-l field and recalls guidance themes such as 34:6 and 34:24; against benefit-for-self formulas such as 10:108, the mechanism here is sharper: guidance reaches the speaker by what the Lord reveals.

topics.headline: perfect state under condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is presented as achieved orientation while still kept from becoming self-congratulation.
topics.reason: The perfect first-person Form VIII verb is inside the second protasis and has no direct object.

topics.headline: Form VIII internalizes guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker comes to guidance but does not author the source of guidance.
topics.reason: The h-d-y route field and Form VIII morphology support received orientation; Form X seeking is not the local form.

topics.headline: h-d-y reverses ḍ-l-l
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second condition reverses the error field while adding the means of guidance beyond formulas such as 10:108.
topics.reason: The rows cite 34:6, 34:24, and 10:108; the local text keeps the opposition and specifies revelation as means.

topics.headline: guided state yields to source clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the syntax shifts attention from “I am guided” to the revealed source that makes guidance possible.
topics.reason: The second apodosis begins with a fronted means phrase before the revelation verb and delayed subject.

words.gloss_range: second result link introducing guidance’s means-first answer
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) marks the answer to the guidance condition, just as the earlier result particle marked the answer to error. This time, however, the payload is not restriction but source: the apodosis opens with {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bimā}}), putting means before the revealing verb. The repeated fāʾ therefore highlights the ayah’s asymmetry: error receives bounded liability; guidance receives revealed causation.

topics.headline: answer begins with means phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance has its own syntactically marked answer, and that answer begins with means rather than a finite verb.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies words 12-17 as the answer to the second protasis.

topics.headline: result fused to instrument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the asymmetry between the two answers: restriction for error, means and causation for guidance.
topics.reason: The written form fuses the result particle with the instrumental preposition, supporting a compact means-first answer.

words.gloss_range: instrumental or causal preposition attaching guidance to what is revealed
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) attaches guidance to means and cause. In {{ar:فَبِمَا}} ({{tr:fa-bimā}}), the bāʾ makes the revealed content or revealing act the medium and ground of guidance, so the speaker’s guided state cannot be parsed as independent self-origin. Because the phrase is fronted before {{ar:يُوحِىٓ}} ({{tr:yūḥī}}) and before {{ar:رَبِّىٓ}} ({{tr:rabbī}}), the means of guidance is heard before the revealer is named.

topics.headline: guidance by revealed means
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is explained through and because of revelation, not from autonomous insight.
topics.reason: The preposition governs mā and relates to the guided state as the means or cause.

topics.headline: result, instrument, content packed together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surface compresses conditional answer, instrument, and broad content into one tight opening.
topics.reason: The bāʾ is attached directly to mā, with fāʾ before it.

topics.headline: means foregrounded before subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause places the means of guidance first, before even naming the Lord as subject.
topics.reason: The local word order is prepositional phrase, revelation verb, recipient, then delayed subject.

words.gloss_range: relative or maṣdariyyah particle holding both revealed content and revealing act in view
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) keeps the means phrase broad. It can route the clause as “what He reveals” or as “His revealing,” so both revealed content and the act of revelation remain available. That breadth does not loosen the source; because {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is inside the fronted {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bimā}}), either reading still makes guidance dependent on the Lord’s communication rather than on the speaker’s independent capacity.

topics.headline: content and act both available
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is not reduced to one item of information; the revealed content and the revealing process both remain in view.
topics.reason: QAC licenses relative or maṣdariyyah force, and the following imperfect revelation verb supports both routes.

topics.headline: broad mā still source-bound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mā is broad but not free-floating: its breadth is bound inside the instrumental phrase that explains guidance.
topics.reason: The particle stands in the fronted bi-phrase before the revealing verb.

words.gloss_range: active imperfect revelation verb with recipient before delayed subject
words.root_gloss_range: swift, subtle, targeted communication and revelation; local Form IV selects directed sending from the Lord
words.prose: {{ar:يُوحِىٓ}} ({{tr:yūḥī}}) is the live revelation mechanism of the guidance clause. Its imperfect form keeps the revealing act active after the completed conditional states, and its active Form IV shape presents directed sending, not vague insight or negotiated signaling. The word order lets the act and recipient appear before the delayed subject {{ar:رَبِّىٓ}} ({{tr:rabbī}}), so the movement of revelation toward the speaker is heard before the revealer is named; together with {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) and {{ar:سَمِيعٌۭ}} ({{tr:samīʿun}}), it forms the ayah’s communication chain, with 42:51 supporting waḥy as a divine communication mode.

topics.headline: imperfect active revealing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance rests on an active, ongoing revealing act whose subject will be named, not on an anonymous passive event.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an active imperfect third-person verb with the delayed subject later supplied.

topics.headline: waḥy as targeted communication
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that revelation is subtle and targeted but also intentional and one-way from the Lord, not mutual signaling or private inference.
topics.reason: The local Form IV verb and recipient phrase select directed revelation while excluding reciprocal forms.

topics.headline: verb and recipient before subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause tracing revelation toward the speaker before naming the Lord as source.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the recipient phrase before the delayed subject.

topics.headline: say, reveal, hear
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 34:50 is built through communication: commanded speech, divine revealing, and divine hearing, with 42:51 supporting waḥy as divine communication mode.
topics.reason: The local surfaces include saying, revealing, and hearing; cited parallels support the communication frame without inventing a new local sense.

words.gloss_range: directional recipient phrase marking the speaker as endpoint of revelation
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَىَّ}} ({{tr:ilayya}}) supplies the recipient endpoint for {{ar:يُوحِىٓ}} ({{tr:yūḥī}}). The first-person suffix makes the speaker the target of revelation, not its origin and not the addressee as recipient. Placed between the verb and {{ar:رَبِّىٓ}} ({{tr:rabbī}}), the phrase foregrounds the path of communication toward me, and the final {{ar:قَرِيبٌۭ}} ({{tr:qarībun}}) answers that direction by naming the revealer as near.

topics.headline: speaker receives revelation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same first-person speaker who bears error receives guidance as directed communication.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the ilā phrase as the recipient complement of the revelation verb.

topics.headline: endpoint fused to speaker identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that revelation is directed to “me,” not to the audience or an unspecified recipient.
topics.reason: The preposition plus first-person suffix is a single fused recipient phrase.

topics.headline: toward me answered by near
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the directed movement of revelation is completed by the closing claim of nearness.
topics.reason: The phrase intervenes before the delayed subject, and the final predicate supplies the proximity answer.

words.gloss_range: my Lord as the definite delayed subject and source of revealed guidance
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, mastery, nurture, sustaining rule, and bringing to completion; local construct selects personal Lord-relation
words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّىٓ}} ({{tr:rabbī}}) finally names the revealer after the verb and recipient have traced the path of revelation. As a possessed noun, it is definite without an article and relational to the speaker; the Lord is not an abstract authority but “my Lord” as source. The r-b-b field makes the revealed guidance formative governance, combining rule, nurture, ownership, and completion. Its first-person suffix balances {{ar:نَفْسِى}} ({{tr:nafsī}}): my self receives the burden of error, while my Lord supplies guidance by revelation, and the return from 34:48 shifts the same Lord-reference from truth’s force to guidance’s source. The rabbī/rabbiya yāʾ variation affects liaison sound without loosening that possessive bond.

topics.headline: Lord named after path of revelation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Lordship crowns the revealed act after the communication has been traced toward the speaker.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies rabbī as the delayed subject of the revelation verb.

topics.headline: revelation as nurturing rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the source of guidance is sustaining, governing Lordship, not merely an information sender.
topics.reason: The r-b-b root field supports nurture, rule, ownership, and completion; the local noun names a standing Lord-relation.

topics.headline: my self versus my Lord
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the shared first-person suffix sharpens opposite roles: personal liability for error and personal dependence on Lordly revelation for guidance.
topics.reason: The same speaker is linked to nafsī and rabbī, but the syntax assigns burden to the self and source to the Lord.

topics.headline: same-surah Lord-reference narrows
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the broad Lordship of 1:2 and the nearby Lord-reference of 34:48 are narrowed here into the personal source of revelation.
topics.reason: The rows cite 1:2 and 34:48; local grammar keeps the subject as the Lord who reveals.

topics.headline: recitational yāʾ variation leaves relation intact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that yāʾ realization affects liaison sound but not the possessive Lord-relation anchoring the guidance clause.
topics.reason: Accepted recitational variation is relevant to surface realization, but it does not alter the local possessive syntax.

words.gloss_range: emphatic pronoun clause resuming the revealer for the final predicates
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:innahu}}) converts the two conditional frames into an emphatic nominal seal. The pronoun resumes {{ar:رَبِّىٓ}} ({{tr:rabbī}}), so the final predicates do not float generically and do not refer back to the self; they belong to the revealer. By gathering the source before {{ar:سَمِيعٌۭ}} ({{tr:samīʿun}}) and {{ar:قَرِيبٌۭ}} ({{tr:qarībun}}), the word validates the whole argument: the Lord who reveals is the one described as hearing and near, and the pronoun closes the Lord-reference thread after the truth-arrival frame of 34:49.

topics.headline: attributes routed to my Lord
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing attributes are attached to the revealer, not to an unspecified subject or to the speaker’s self.
topics.reason: Attachment cross-references resolve the pronoun to rabbī, and the following predicates attach to the inna clause.

topics.headline: conditional logic grounded in assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from suspended conditionals to emphatic assertion, grounding both halves in divine attributes.
topics.reason: The inna plus pronoun opens the final nominal clause after the two conditional structures.

topics.headline: prior Lord-reference compressed into attributes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pronoun closes the Lord-reference thread from the preceding truth-arrival frame into this ayah’s attribute seal.
topics.reason: The boundary rows are compatible with local pronoun resolution to rabbī and with the final predicate pair.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative intensive predicate of hearing
words.root_gloss_range: hearing, heeding, receiving sound or report; local predicate makes hearing a stable attribute
words.prose: {{ar:سَمِيعٌۭ}} ({{tr:samīʿun}}) is the first predicate of the closing seal, coordinated with {{ar:قَرِيبٌۭ}} ({{tr:qarībun}}) rather than modifying it. Its indefinite nominative and intensive adjective form make hearing a stable qualitative attribute, not merely one moment of hearing. After {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) and {{ar:يُوحِىٓ}} ({{tr:yūḥī}}), the s-m-ʿ field closes the communication chain: the Lord who reveals toward the speaker also hears the speech the speaker is commanded to say, a pattern resonant with 58:1.

topics.headline: first predicate in paired seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hearing is a full predicate before nearness, not a modifier swallowed by the second attribute.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks samīʿun as the first predicate of innahu and qarībun as the second.

topics.headline: hearing as durable capacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hearing is presented as a standing attribute rather than a single event or merely a definite-name formula.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an intensive adjective, indefinite nominative, as the predicate.

topics.headline: speech and revelation under divine hearing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that commanded speech and hidden revelation are both enclosed by divine hearing, with 58:1 offering a concrete speech-heard parallel.
topics.reason: The local communication chain includes saying, revealing, and hearing; the root field supports hearing, heeding, and receiving report.

topics.headline: shared tanwīn seals attributes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the two final predicates sound like a paired attribute seal rather than disconnected labels.
topics.reason: The paired final tanwīn is present on both predicates and reinforces their coordinate status.

words.gloss_range: second indefinite nominative predicate of nearness
words.root_gloss_range: spatial, temporal, relational, and responsive nearness; local adjective states proximity as already true
words.prose: {{ar:قَرِيبٌۭ}} ({{tr:qarībun}}) completes the final predicate pair as a coordinate attribute of the revealer. The q-r-b field answers the direction of {{ar:إِلَىَّ}} ({{tr:ilayya}}): revelation comes toward the speaker from a Lord who is not remote from the endpoint, with 2:186 giving a concrete nearness-invocation parallel. Its adjective form states nearness as already true, not as an event of becoming near. As the ayah’s last word, it lets the command that began with {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) land on proximity, while echoes into 34:51 keep q-r-b pressure alive beyond the verse boundary.

topics.headline: nearness completes predicate pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that nearness is a second full predicate of the revealer, complementing hearing rather than replacing it.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks qarībun as the second predicate of innahu.

topics.headline: toward me met by nearness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the directed revelation of ilayya is answered by responsive proximity, with 2:186 giving a concrete nearness-invocation parallel.
topics.reason: The local direction phrase and final nearness predicate are connected by the row evidence and supported by the q-r-b semantic range.

topics.headline: nearness as standing quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the close does not narrate God approaching; it states nearness as already in force.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a qualitative adjective predicate rather than an eventive verb.

topics.headline: command lands on nearness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is framed from commanded speech to nearness, and that 34:51 keeps the q-r-b sound-field active at the boundary.
topics.reason: The word is the ayah’s endpoint, shares cadence with samīʿun, and has same-surah boundary uptake in 34:51.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired conditionals "إن ضللت...على نفسي" and "وإن اهتديت فبما يوحي إلي ربي" assign opposite causal accounts to error and guidance.
baseline_models.mechanism: Deviation leaves the intended path and lands on the speaker's own self, while guidance is credited to a hidden divine communication delivered under formative Lordship. Hearing and nearness keep that asymmetric account relational rather than fatalistic.

activation_trace.role: Departure from guidance and intended direction supplies the negative path mechanism.
The self as the very identity of the thing localizes the loss in the speaker rather than exporting it.
Gentle indication toward path and truth supplies the positive reorientation.
Divine report and inspiration identify the credited source of reorientation.
Repair, nurture, and completion make Lordship the formative agency behind guidance.
Actual hearing makes the declaration answerable to an attentive addressee.
Nearness removes remoteness between the speaking subject and the source who hears.

changed_reading.before: If the speaker errs, he bears it; if he is guided, revelation causes it.
changed_reading.after: The verse is an asymmetric causal ledger: path-loss is charged to the speaker's own identity, while recovered direction is received from the nearby, hearing Lord who forms and completes him.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The contrast between "ضللت" and "بما يوحي إلي" joins loss or disappearance to a communication that arrives in concealment.
baseline_models.mechanism: The error side can be modeled as losing an object, location, or retained trace; the guidance side supplies a subtle signal that restores orientation. Hearing and nearness describe a short communication circuit even though the transmitted knowledge is hidden.

activation_trace.role: Disappearance and concealment recast error as becoming unavailable to orientation.
Loss of a thing or its location supplies the missing-position problem.
Loss of retention adds a memory or signal-failure mode to straying.
Guidance resolves the lost-position problem by indicating the route and truth.
Knowledge delivered secretly supplies the restoring signal without making it publicly self-generated.
A subtle voice gives the hidden delivery an acoustic edge.
Hearing supplies reception at the far end of the signal relation.
Nearness makes recovery a low-distance relation rather than a remote search.

changed_reading.before: Error is a wrong belief, whereas revelation supplies the right belief.
changed_reading.after: Error is also loss of position, visibility, or retention; revelation is the nearby hidden signal by which a lost subject is located and reoriented.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The imperative "قل" turns a first-person account of receiving revelation into an overt utterance.
baseline_models.mechanism: A hidden communication is not retained as private interior knowledge: the commanded speaker voices it, names his own possible failure, and submits the result to the One who hears. The speaking self is therefore a conduit and accountable receiver, not the autonomous origin of the claim.

activation_trace.role: Bringing speech out by articulation turns the conditional into a public act.
The self's intention and discernment locate the internal point at which reception can fail or take hold.
Hidden impartation supplies what precedes and authorizes the overt speech.
Hearing as understanding and compliance makes reception answerable in action, not only audible.

changed_reading.before: The speaker reports his private epistemic condition.
changed_reading.after: The verse performs a conversion from hidden reception to commanded public speech, with the speaker openly owning failure while refusing authorship of guidance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah first supplies vertical delivery, then explicitly aligns what is sent down from the Lord with stable truth, guidance, and a straight road. This turns the focus verse's "بما يوحي" from a generic source claim into a transport sequence whose delivered content becomes traversable orientation.

activation_trace.role: Descent and arrival place downward delivery inside the surah's opening circulation pattern.
Caused descent and conveyance identify the content as something delivered to the addressee.
Truth as stable correspondence marks the delivered content as reality-bearing.
Gentle indication converts delivered truth into directional guidance.
The straight road gives the directional result a traversable form.
The focus revelation is the local receiving point of that delivered truth-route.

structural_cues: 34:2 sequences entering, exiting, descending, and ascending; 34:6 sequences what is sent down from the Lord, truth, guidance, and road.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies delivery, truth, guidance, and road in sequence; I supply the causal arrow from delivered content to verified orientation. A live alternative is that 34:6 coordinates attributes without specifying process stages.

changed_reading.before: The speaker is guided because his Lord reveals something to him.
changed_reading.after: Guidance is the terminal effect of a delivery chain: content descends, proves reality-bearing, and opens a road that the receiver can follow.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated commands to say, followed by the focus's own "قل", make the first-person conditional one commissioned segment in a surah-wide speech chain. The exchange "What did your Lord say? ... the truth" further identifies utterance as a carrier of reality rather than self-originating opinion.

activation_trace.role: An opposing assertion and the answering command establish a recurring public speech contest.
The repeated acts of saying form a relay that asks after and reports the Lord's speech.
Stable correspondence with reality is the reported content at the end of the relay.
The command to articulate immediately precedes the focus and continues the commission.
A second adjacent command makes the focus's opening imperative part of a concentrated sequence.
The focus utterance is voiced under the same commission rather than initiated as autobiography.

structural_cues: The packet repeats "قل" across 34:3, 22, 24-27, 30, 36, 39, and 46-50, with three consecutive commands at 34:48-50.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated imperatives and the Lord-speech/truth exchange; I infer that repetition subordinates the first-person voice to a commission. The alternative is to treat each imperative as only a local discourse marker.

changed_reading.before: The speaker independently qualifies his own possibility of error and guidance.
changed_reading.after: The speaker is instructed to voice his own fallibility; the very sentence that denies self-authorship of guidance is itself an enacted piece of received guidance.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier formulations place people inside far error and contrast being upon guidance with being inside clear error. The focus shifts to "أضل على نفسي": error is no longer only an enclosing region but a consequence loaded onto the self, while the guidance clause marks its enabling source with "بما".

activation_trace.role: Departure from guidance supplies the enclosing state named by the verse's "in" construction.
Distance from nearness stretches that error field away from access.
Path indication supports the construction of being upon a directional footing.
Straying again supplies the alternative containing field.
Manifestness makes the error field exposed rather than merely obscure.
The focus repeats path departure but changes its local grammatical relation.
The self as one's very identity becomes the bearer of the result.
Reorientation remains the opposed directional state, now explicitly source-enabled.

structural_cues: 34:8 has "في الضلال البعيد", 34:24 has "لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين", and 34:50 has "أضل على نفسي" opposed to "فبما يوحي".
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated spatial prepositions and their changes; I treat container, footing, burden, and means as functional spatial roles. These prepositions may alternatively be conventional idioms with less mechanical force.

changed_reading.before: Error and guidance are simply opposite states.
changed_reading.after: The surah relocates their mechanics: guidance is a footing reached through supplied indication, error is an enclosing distance, and its realized cost is laid upon the erring self.

context_deltas.mechanism: A visible, measured itinerary is made available for secure travel; the travelers request that its stages be pushed farther apart, wrong themselves, and are scattered. This gives "ضللت على نفسي" an enacted route model: self-harm occurs by converting accessible orientation into remoteness until the traveling collective loses coherence.

activation_trace.role: Prominence and disclosure make the route's stations inspectable rather than hidden.
Deliberate measured arrangement supplies the route's usable spacing.
Going and flowing turn the arrangement into a traversable itinerary.
Actively causing distance is the requested modification that breaks accessibility.
Their own identities are named as the immediate objects of the resulting wrong.
Tearing into dispersed pieces supplies the terminal loss of route and group coherence.
Loss of a thing or its place names the focus outcome of the remoteness sequence.

structural_cues: 34:18 moves through visible settlements with measured travel in safety; 34:19 requests greater distance, names self-wrong, and ends in complete scattering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a prepared route, chosen remoteness, self-wrong, and dispersal; I infer a causal route-degradation sequence. A live alternative is that the distance request expresses ingratitude without defining straying itself.

changed_reading.before: To stray against oneself is to choose a wrong direction.
changed_reading.after: It can be the infrastructural act of making a usable route remote: the subject degrades its own access until both location and communal coherence are lost.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context depicts following another, being diverted from guidance, and receiving coercive commands. Those are real social causes of error, yet guilt remains attached to agents. Thus "على نفسي" marks non-transferable loss and liability, not an assertion that no one can influence another.

activation_trace.role: Following behind another supplies a genuine external pathway into error.
Turning and diverting name the accused social interference with access.
Path indication is the object from which the vulnerable claim they were diverted.
Guilt and offense keep agency attached to those who answered the pressure.
Demand and compulsion supply a second concrete mechanism of social influence.
The self remains the terminal bearer even within a network of influence.

structural_cues: 34:31-33 stages reciprocal blame between the weak and arrogant, including obstruction, night-and-day plotting, and commands; neither side succeeds in transferring the final account.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies following, diversion, commands, and retained guilt; I infer a distinction between causal influence and final liability. The alternative is to read "على نفسي" as both internally caused and internally borne, but the social scenes make that stronger exclusivity difficult.

changed_reading.before: My straying is solely self-caused and concerns no external agent.
changed_reading.after: Others can pressure, divert, and command, but the realized loss cannot be assigned away: "upon myself" fixes consequence without denying social causation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Wealth and descendants are denied the power to transport their possessors into privileged proximity. The focus's "قريب" therefore first names the Lord's own availability as hearer and source, not a rank manufactured by assets or lineage; human standing is a separate responsive relation.

activation_trace.role: Accumulated wealth supplies the rejected means of purchasing proximity.
Lineal offspring supply the rejected means of inheriting proximity.
Caused nearness names the transport that possessions and descendants cannot perform.
Proximity as standing or station identifies the status at issue in the denial.
Hearing makes the focus nearness immediately communicative.
The Lord's nearness is asserted directly, before any asset can mediate it.

structural_cues: 34:37 denies that wealth or children bring people near, then distinguishes belief and fitting action; 34:50 predicates hearing and nearness directly of the Lord.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two uses of proximity and a rejected material transport; I distinguish source-availability from acquired human station. A live alternative is that both passages use one status relation viewed from opposite sides.

changed_reading.before: "Near" is a general assurance of divine closeness.
changed_reading.after: It denies the need for a purchased or inherited access mechanism: the revealer-hearer is already near, while favored standing concerns how recipients answer that access.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding instruction combines warning, deliberate standing, paired and solitary configurations, and repeated inward thought. Against that method, the focus conditional reads as disciplined self-testing: the speaker permits the hypothesis of his own error while locating positive orientation in revelation rather than claiming automatic personal certainty.

activation_trace.role: Fear-awakening reminder supplies the stakes that initiate examination.
Resolved rising to the task supplies deliberate readiness rather than passive opinion.
Joining one to one supplies a paired checking configuration.
The isolated individual supplies an independent checking configuration.
The heart's repeated movement through a matter supplies active reconsideration.
Intention and discernment within the self become the object of the diagnostic.
Hidden impartation supplies the external calibration that prevents self-testing from becoming self-authorizing.

structural_cues: 34:46 orders standing for God in pairs and singly and then thinking; 34:50 uses parallel first-person conditionals rather than an unqualified claim of personal correctness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an examination procedure and a conditional self-account; I infer that the latter models the posture requested by the former. The alternative is that 34:46 addresses opponents only and does not describe the speaker's stance.

changed_reading.before: The conditional is a rhetorical concession about possible error.
changed_reading.after: It also models an epistemic discipline: expose the self to examination, allow its failure to remain live, and credit successful orientation to received calibration.

context_deltas.mechanism: The Lord casts stable truth, whereas opponents cast speech toward the unseen from a distant position and later cannot reach what they claim from afar. The focus sits between these motions and specifies the reliable channel: guidance is received through revelation from a near, hearing source, not projected into hidden reality from distance.

activation_trace.role: Casting supplies forceful outward delivery, here carrying truth from the knowledgeable Lord.
Stable correspondence with reality qualifies the content of the divine casting.
Reaching by extension names the access that a distant position no longer permits.
Distance from nearness blocks belated access.
Throwing speech supplies the counter-motion of unsupported verbal projection.
What is screened from sight is the target about which the distant speech projects.
Remoteness diagnoses the projectors' lack of epistemic access.
Secretly delivered knowledge supplies reception rather than projection.
Hearing makes the reliable channel reciprocal and answerable.
Nearness is the decisive opposite of the distance from which unseen claims are hurled.

structural_cues: 34:48 has the Lord casting truth as knower of unseen things; 34:50 credits guidance to revelation and closes with hearing-nearness; 34:52-53 repeat failed reaching and casting from a distant place.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mirrored casting, hidden reality, failed reaching, and near/far poles; I infer an epistemic contrast between reception and projection. The alternative is that the repeated casting is rhetorical wordplay without a technical account of knowledge.

changed_reading.before: Revelation is one true information source among false assertions.
changed_reading.after: The coda maps two opposed epistemic motions: truth arrives through a near receptive channel, while error throws speech at hidden reality from a location too distant to reach it.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately after the focus, there is no escape and seizure comes from a near place; the closing barrier then separates people from what they desire. "سميع قريب" therefore carries a juridical edge alongside reassurance: speech and deviation are already within hearing range and enforcement distance.

activation_trace.role: Failure to escape or remain unreachable removes any latency in consequence.
Seizure and capture turn proximity into operative jurisdiction.
The near place supplies the short range from which capture occurs.
An intervening barrier supplies the final irreversible separation.
Hearing places every voiced claim within cognizance before enforcement.
Nearness makes divine cognizance operational rather than merely affective.

structural_cues: 34:50 ends "Hearing, Near"; 34:51 immediately negates escape and describes seizure from a near place; 34:54 ends with an imposed barrier.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, hearing, near seizure, and final separation; I infer that proximity compresses the interval between cognizance and consequence. The live alternative is that divine nearness in 34:50 is purely consolatory and 34:51 uses unrelated spatial language.

changed_reading.before: "Hearing, Near" comforts the speaker that revelation and prayer are attended.
changed_reading.after: It also warns that error cannot create jurisdictional distance: the One who hears is already close enough for consequence to arrive without escape.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The nourishment-and-growth image comes through the packet's secondary mapping of ر ب ب to ر ب و, so it is form-distant and must not replace the direct Lordship sense. It remains anchored to "ربي" and is reinforced by the primary repair-and-upbringing branch; downstream prose should label it a cultivation analogy, not a lexical gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The possessive "ربي" names the source whose revelation produces the speaker's guidance.

activation_trace.role: Repair, upbringing, and stagewise completion supply the primary formative mechanism.
Nourishment and growth extend formative Lordship into an exploratory cultivation image.
A gentle gift makes guidance something bestowed for development rather than extracted by the self.
Divine inspiration supplies what is fed into that developmental process.
Lordship appears in the flourishing settlement scene and supports care that can be answered or refused.
Turning one's side away supplies refusal of the cultivating relation.
Replacement of one yield by another supplies the changed fruit of refusal.

changed_reading.before: The Lord transmits correct information that guides the speaker.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, revelation is also formative intake: the Lord cultivates orientation stage by stage, while turning away changes what the life under cultivation yields.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The water-seeking and waterskin branches of ق ر ب are concrete cross-domain images, not the ordinary predication of "قريب" here. They remain anchored to the exact focus root and become coherent with the surah's measured journeys and failed reaching; downstream prose should present this only as a logistics analogy for access to sustaining revelation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The closing "قريب" is the point at which the focus explicitly negates distance from the revealer.

activation_trace.role: Night travel toward a water source turns nearness into reachable supply.
The water container makes proximity portable as a held reserve.
Hidden delivery supplies the sustaining content carried through the access analogy.
Traversable movement through measured stages supplies the logistics frame.
Deliberately increasing distance makes the sustaining source harder to reach.
Failed extension toward a distant object supplies the terminal access failure.

changed_reading.before: The Lord is spatially or relationally close.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, revelation is a sustaining source already within reach; straying consists in redesigning the journey until the source can no longer be reached or carried.

strongest_changes: The repeated "قل" sequence turns the focus's first-person humility into commissioned revelation in action.
The surah's route grammar moves from visible measured access to chosen remoteness and self-fragmentation, giving "على نفسي" an infrastructural mechanism.
Social following, obstruction, and commands revise self-liability into non-transferable consequence without denying external influence.
The final casting and distance pattern opposes near reception of hidden knowledge to unsupported projection at the unseen, while near seizure adds an immediate jurisdictional edge.
summary.what_was_special: The focus condenses the surah's speech, route, and distance systems into one asymmetric conditional: the self owns path-loss, but not the production of guidance; hidden content becomes voiced through a nearby hearing relation.
remaining_uncertainties: The force assigned to "على", "في", and "بما" may exceed ordinary idiomatic syntax even though the repeated spatial pattern supports it.
"سميع قريب" can sustain both consolatory access and immediate jurisdiction; the context does not require choosing one.
The cultivation and water-access readings depend on form-distant or cross-domain branch images and should remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Error terminates locally; guidance arrives through a hidden channel.** `ض ل ل/B001` is straying, `ن ف س/B012` the thing itself, `ه د ي/B002` intended direction, `و ح ي/B001` hidden imparting of knowledge, `س م ع/B003` understanding and compliance, and `ق ر ب/B001` nearness. The conditional asymmetry assigns error to the self but guidance to received revelation. The self is error’s terminal account; hidden imparting supplies directional input; hearing and nearness keep the channel responsive. The packet gives attribution; I infer that guidance is relational reception without transferring blame for error. The ayah reads agency as asymmetric but coherent: liability remains local while orientation is received.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 34:51 turned the closing `قريب` from receptive nearness into immediate capture, showing that proximity intensifies whichever relation one has formed rather than guaranteeing comfort.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Near hearing as the condition for successful hidden communication.** `و ح ي B001` supplies hidden imparting of knowledge, `س م ع B003` understanding and compliance, and `ق ر ب B001` nearness against distance. Guidance is attributed to what the Lord communicates, then hearing and nearness close the line; 34:51 has capture from a near place, while 34:53 has uninformed casting from a far place. The branches assign revelation the channel, hearing reception, and nearness reliable relation. The packet supplies the near/far contrast; I infer that hidden communication succeeds through receptive proximity, not guesswork. Guidance reads as an active communication relation.

2. **Error collapses inward while guidance arrives from beyond the self.** `ض ل ل B002` supplies hiddenness or disappearance, `ن ف س B012` the very thing itself, and `ه د ي B001` guidance toward truth. The two conditions are asymmetrical: error is restricted `عَلَىٰ نَفْسِى`, while guidance is sourced in revelation. The branches assign disappearance the self-contained loss and guidance an incoming directional role. The packet supplies this grammar; I infer that responsibility for deviation cannot be exported, whereas guidance is received rather than self-generated. The ayah reads as an asymmetry of liability and source.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 34:51-53 clarified that `قَرِيبٌ` is epistemic as well as spatial: effective seizure comes from near, while claims cast from far miss the hidden. The sequence confirmed revelation as receptive nearness rather than remote speculation.

baseline.text: De ki: ‘Saparsam ancak kendi aleyhime saparım. Doğru yolu bulursam bu, Rabbimin bana vahyettiği sayesindedir. O işitendir, yakındır.’

findings.text: Sapma kendi hesabında son bulurken doğru yön dışarıdan gelen vahiy yoluyla alınır; sorumluluk başkasına aktarılamaz, fakat yöneliş de benliğin kendi üretimi sayılmaz.
Görülmeyen iletişimin başarı koşulu, uzak tahmin değil, vahyi anlayarak işiten yakın ve karşılıklı bir ilişkidir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P4: Truth Behaves as Effective One-Way Transmission
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Truth originates beyond the speaker, is projected effectively into the scene, and can be received as near guidance; falsehood lacks both generative beginning and productive return.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Projectile force, recurrence, revelation, hearing, and nearness form a transmission model in which efficacy depends on valid origin rather than rhetorical possession.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Guidance Received From Near
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Error falls back upon the self, while guidance arrives through concealed divine communication whose source hears at close range.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: departure from guidance (`quranic:root_000913:B001/m01`), the self as bearer of consequence (`quranic:root_001533:B012/m01`), guidance toward the route (`quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`), divine hidden communication (`quranic:root_001633:B004/m01`), hearing (`quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`), relational nearness (`quranic:root_001212:B001/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The verse separates ownership of error from receipt of guidance. Revelation traverses hidden distance without becoming remote because hearing and nearness characterize its source.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı sesle ortaya çıkarılan söz ve harflerden kurulu sözlü ifade olarak verir. Geçici çerçeve aynı çekirdeği taşıyor; dil organı, hükümdar unvanı ve mecazi yan kullanımlar bu dalın dışında kalır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sayı, miktar ya da ölçü bakımından çok olmayışını bildirir. Bundan yoksulluk ve düşüklük, bir şeyi az sayma veya az gösterme ve belirli yapılarda hiçlik ya da seyrek gerçekleşme anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar azlığın temel sayı ve miktar karşıtlığında birleşir; yoksulluk ve düşüklük, az sayma ve bazı yapılarda yokluğa yaklaşan kullanım bu çekirdeğin düzenli uzantılarıdır.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar iri bir küp veya büyük kap üzerinde birleşir; tanınmış bölgesel kaplar büyüklüğü örnekler, iki kaplık kullanım ise nesne adını kapasite ölçüsüne taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Taşıma, yükselme ve yüklenerek yola koyulma bu kolun sınırıdır; salt sayısal azlık bu anlamlara katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yük taşıma ile yükselme çekirdek çizgileri ayrılır; ağır bulut taşıma, uçuşa kalkma ve yolcuların ayrılması yalnızca kendi özne ve yapılarında geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi korku veya öfke yüzünden tutan titreme ve silkinişi açıkça tanımlar; genel hareket kararsızlığı değil, duygusal tetikleyicisi bulunan bedensel bir sarsıntı söz konusudur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol insanda korku veya öfkeyle beliren titremeyle sınırlıdır; nesnelerin genel sallanma ve yerinde duramama hali ayrı koldadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

error_profile.preserves: Korku veya öfke koşulunu ve bunun doğurduğu bedensel titremeyi birlikte korur.

error_profile.preserves: Öfke nedenini ve onunla birlikte ortaya çıkan titremeyi korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol genel fiziksel oynama, kararsızlık ve hareket sesiyle ilgilidir; korku veya öfkeden doğan insana özgü titreme değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak kolun hareket ettirme, sallanma, yerinde duramama ve hareket sesi anlamlarını kapsar; özel bir yapının anlamı genelleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi hareket ettirerek yerinden oynatmayı ve onun kararsızca sallanıp bulunduğu yerde duramamasını bildirir; bu hareketin çıkardığı ses de aynı olayın işitsel yönüdür.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi hareket ettirip onun yerinden oynamasına ve sarsılmasına neden olmaktır.
Nesnenin bulunduğu yerde sabit kalmayıp sallanması, oynaması veya düzensiz hareket etmesidir.
Sallanma ve yer değiştirme sırasında çıkan ses, hareket olayının işitsel belirtisi olarak adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar dışarıdan hareket ettirme ile nesnenin kararsızca sallanıp yerinde duramaması üzerinde birleşir; hareketin sesi bu fiziksel olayın ayrılmaz işitsel belirtisi olarak eklenir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, anlamın çekirdeğini amaçtan, doğru yoldan ve doğruluktan ayrılma olarak kurar; hem yolunu bulamama hem de yanlış ve boş işlere yönelme bu çekirdeğin gerçekleşmeleridir. Başkasını doğru yoldan uzaklaştıran ettirgen kullanım da aynı anlam alanına bağlıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal fiziksel olarak gözden yitme, bir şeyi kaybetme, unutma ya da kayıp hayvan adı olma anlamlarını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın sapma çekirdeğini korur; yol, arazi, kişiyi sapmış sayma ve bir işi yanlış tutumla yapma gibi kalıba bağlı kullanımları ayrı yüzler olarak sınırlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir kimsenin amaçtan, doğru yoldan veya doğruluktan ayrılması, yolunu bulamaması ya da yanlış ve boş olana yönelmesidir. Ettirgen kullanımda başka biri bu doğrultudan uzaklaştırılır.

facets.statement: Amaçtan, doğru yoldan veya doğruluktan ayrılma ve uygun yönü bulamama anlamın temelidir.
Yanlış, asılsız veya boş işlere yönelme, yönsel sapmanın düşünce ve davranış alanındaki uzantısıdır.
